question: How should an intelligent advisor system be designed so that knowledge graphs and LLMs combine their complementary strengths in knowledge representation and reasoning?
contributions: A mental model of an intelligent system as knowledge bases plus reasoning engines
A comparison of KG and LLM knowledge acquisition and reasoning
A purpose-driven (CRISP-DM based) approach to KG construction

results.claim: Wu et al. tested 11 task types and found LLM performance on counterfactual variants of familiar tasks degraded substantially and consistently versus default conditions.
results.setup: Suite of tasks from coding to drawing, logic to spatial, chess to arithmetic; counterfactual variants vs default tasks; no scores given in chapter

results.setup: Single prompt (Listing 2.1, text not extracted) to Claude.ai 3.5 Sonnet; anecdotal, authors expect different result with newer models
results.note: Answer text is in Fig 2.9 image, not extracted

results.claim: Authors report from experience that bottom-up KG construction often leads to failure of KG adoption.

limits: No experiments beyond one anecdotal prompt to Claude 3.5 Sonnet; authors say results will differ by print time.
Design concepts only, no quantitative evaluation of hybrid KG+LLM systems.
Figure contents (e.g. Fig 2.9 answer, Fig 2.11 arrows) are images and not in the text.
practices: Decompose an intelligent system into knowledge representation and reasoning components (sec 2.1).
Build intelligent advisor systems (suggest, not act) when users keep final decisions (sec 2.2.2).
Give an intelligent system a meaningful objective, an intelligent experience, continuous knowledge update, and orchestration (sec 2.2.3).
Use KGs for precise rule-based reasoning and LLMs for pattern recognition, ambiguity and incomplete information (sec 2.4).
Start KG construction from business objectives (CRISP-DM revisited), not by importing all available data (sec 2.6).
On later iterations extend the KG by difference, using its schemaless flexibility, without breaking earlier data (sec 2.6).

terms.definition: Intelligent systems connect users to AI and ML to achieve meaningful objectives. An intelligent system is one in which intelligence evolves and improves over time, particularly when it improves by watching how users interact with the system.
the "language" that AI systems use to structure, encode, and communicate information about the domain they are modelling
the cognitive process of analyzing information, applying rules, and drawing conclusions based on evidence or premises
provides information and recommendations; does not execute actions on its own
begins with a general statement or hypothesis and examines the possibilities to reach a specific, logical conclusion
makes broad generalizations from specific observations
a formula for estimating an unknown value of interest: the target
flexibility of storing data with fewer (or no) constraints on how data items are formatted and related to each other
